skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Verification discipline for completion claims. Use when about to assert success, claim a fix is complete, report tests passing, or before commits and PRs. Enforces evidence-first workflow.
skill.summary: Requires fresh verification evidence before claiming work is complete.
skill.author: CodingCossack

content.value_statement: Completion claims can be wrong when agents rely on memory or confidence. This skill requires fresh evidence before reporting success.
actual_capabilities: Requires identifying a verification command before making completion claims.
Defines evidence expectations for tests, lint, builds, bug fixes, and requirements.
Encourages reading command output and exit codes before reporting results.
Flags risky phrases such as should, probably, and seems to before verification.
Provides patterns for regression testing, checklist review, and agent delegation checks.
limitations: Does not determine whether a project command is safe to run.
Does not replace domain-specific test, build, or deployment procedures.
Cannot prove correctness when the available verification is incomplete.
Requires the agent or user to choose appropriate verification commands.

use_cases.title: Validate Coding Agent Results
use_cases.description: Require command output or a checked diff before accepting an agent completion report.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads reviewing delegated AI work

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Request Updates
use_cases.description: Confirm tests, lint, builds, and requirements before writing a final status update.
use_cases.target_user: Developers using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code

use_cases.title: Enforce Regression Evidence
use_cases.description: Use a red-green verification cycle before claiming that a bug fix is complete.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Verification Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow before a final answer
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you say this task is done, identify the verification command, run it, read the output, and report the exact result.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Test Confirmation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a targeted code change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the verification-before-completion skill for this change. Choose the most specific test or lint command that covers the edited code, run it fresh, and summarize the evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow across tests, lint, and build checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this branch before release. Check tests, lint, build status, and requirement coverage, then list any gaps instead of assuming completion.

prompt_templates.title: Delegated Agent Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow after another agent reports success
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the agent completion report. Inspect the diff, verify the changed behavior independently, and only confirm completion when the evidence supports it.

output_examples.input: The agent says the bug is fixed and all tests pass.
output_examples.output: Recommended response: verify independently. Inspect the changed files, run the relevant regression test, and report the observed result.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to say the build is clean after running only lint.
output_examples.output: Recommended response: lint does not prove the build. Run the build command or state that build verification is still missing.

output_examples.input: A pull request is ready except the requirements were not re-read.
output_examples.output: Recommended response: re-read the checklist, compare each requirement to the implementation, and report any uncovered items.

best_practices: Run fresh verification in the current work session before making success claims.
Match the verification command to the exact claim being made.
Report incomplete or failing verification clearly, with the observed evidence.
anti_patterns: Claiming tests pass based on a previous run or expected behavior.
Treating lint success as proof that build and runtime behavior are correct.
Accepting another agent completion report without checking the diff or outputs.

faq.question: What does this skill help verify?
faq.answer: It helps verify completion claims for tests, lint, builds, bug fixes, regression tests, delegated work, and requirements.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent to choose and run the right verification command when the environment allows it.

faq.question: Can it guarantee that a fix is correct?
faq.answer: No. It improves evidence quality, but correctness still depends on the available tests and review process.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is tool-agnostic and applies to any coding assistant that can inspect changes and run checks.

faq.question: How should failures be reported?
faq.answer: Report the command, exit status, key failure details, and the remaining work instead of claiming success.

faq.question: When should this skill be used?
faq.answer: Use it before final responses, commits, pull requests, release notes, or any message that claims work is complete.
